query: What customer issues create the most support burden?

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: A clean taxonomy of issue types is directly the axis needed to identify which issues drive support burden. Sampled values (billing_error, configuration_error, outage, feature_request, bug) are all sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: product_area
per_column.rationale: Adds a distinct grouping axis (which product surface is generating tickets), complementary to issue_category. Sampled mappings (billing_and_payments, authentication_and_sso, infrastructure_and_platform, ui_and_ux, data_import_export) are well grounded.

per_column.name: operational_impact
per_column.rationale: Severity/impact is a strong axis for quantifying burden. Most samples are sound (full_service_outage, cosmetic_or_minor). Labeling the invoice ticket as blocked_workflow is a mild stretch but defensible given the finance-deadline framing; uses not_present appropriately for silent rows.

per_column.name: user_scope
per_column.rationale: Blast radius (single_user vs entire_tenant) is a genuine driver of burden and gives a useful grouping axis. Samples are well supported (all members of Acme tenant -> entire_tenant; individual reports -> single_user). CSV export as entire_tenant is a reasonable inference.

per_column.name: root_cause_class
per_column.rationale: Root cause is analytically valuable for pinpointing burden sources, and uses not_present for silent rows. However the invoice row is labeled data_migration_artifact with no textual support -- an invented specific where the text only describes a duplicate line item. This is a confident, unwarranted inference that lowers groundedness.

per_column.name: requires_engineering_escalation
per_column.rationale: Escalation routing/need is a real burden signal. The name implies a boolean but values are routing categories (billing_ops, platform_infra, security_team), which is fine. Samples are reasonable readings, though escalation targets are partly inferred rather than stated.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Workaround availability meaningfully affects support burden. partial_workaround (manual sed step) and not_present are well grounded. However asserting no_workaround for rows where the text is silent (e.g., the invoice ticket) is a confident negative not clearly supported, slightly weakening groundedness.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuinely distinct and query-relevant axes -- issue type, product area, impact severity, blast radius, root cause, escalation, and workaround -- each offering real leverage to group and quantify support burden with little redundancy. Groundedness is generally strong: most values are sound extractions or warranted inferences, and silent rows are handled with not_present. The main weakness is a tendency to assert confident specifics on silent rows (root_cause_class inventing data_migration_artifact for the invoice ticket; workaround_available defaulting to no_workaround without textual support), which introduces some ungrounded values.
